content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on time series so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When time series decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
2. Prefer explicit, readable time series solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
3. Keep time series outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
4. When time series guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. Measure before optimizing any time series bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to time series (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Check that time series terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
8. Validate time series outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
9. Before starting time series work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
10. Surface known limitations of a chosen time series approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
11. State assumptions about time series explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop time series edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated time series concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not skip documenting time series assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about time series over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
